newsitem.title: UK: Engestrom says quits M&G for Liberty Re.
newsitem.headline: Engestrom says quits M&G for Liberty Re.

text.p: John Engestrom told Reuters on Thursday he had left reinsurer M&G, which was acquired last year by Swiss Re, to join Liberty Mutual Group as chief executive officer of Liberty Re.
John Coomber has taken over as head of the new life and health division of Swiss Re, a spokeswoman for M&G Re told Reuters. Engestrom was chief executive of M&G.
Coomber has been appointed to the executive board of Swiss Re, which is pressing ahead with the integration of M&G's operations into the Swiss parent group.

Engestrom, who left M&G on January 17, told Reuters in a telephone interview that he will take up his new post on February 1 with a remit to develop Liberty Re as a composite reinsurer of general, life and health insurance.

His first task will be to obtain authorisation from the Department of Trade & Industry (DTI) for Liberty Re to operate. More information on the intentions and philosphy for Liberty Re will be issued shortly, Engestrom said.

Boston based Liberty Mutual Group had revenue of $8.9 billion in 1995, assets of $37 billion and a surplus of $4.7 billion. It is among the top ten property casualty insurers in the U.S., Engestrom said.
Engestrom said plans to set up a London-based reinsurer formed part of Liberty Mutual's strategy of geographical diversification and more efficient use of capital.

"This is an opportunity to create a state of the art reinsurer. I couldn't have more fun anywhere in the business," he said, adding that his departure from Swiss Re had been on amicable terms after putting in place the timetable and structure for the integration of M&G Re.
Last September, Engestrom said he was in talks with Swiss Re about his longer term future with the group.
Engestrom was widely credited with having returned the ailing life reinsurance group, a part of Prudential Corp Plc until last August, to profit before it was sold to Swiss Re for 1.75 billion stg.
Liberty Mutual had considered launching a London-based reinsurer in 1995, but eventually decided to put the plans on the shelf, Engestrom said.
A spokeswoman for the DTI would neither confirm nor deny that it had received an application to authorise Liberty Re as a reinsurer in 1995.
